Short answer: Businesses open to the public should make their online goods and services accessible. Start by fixing real barriers and combine automated checks with manual testing.

What this means for your business

The U.S. Department of Justice says inaccessible web content can deny people equal access and lists practical considerations such as contrast, headings, keyboard use, and meaningful error cues. This page is not legal advice.

What to watch

  • Buttons or menus that need a mouse.
  • Forms with missing labels or unclear errors.
  • Text that cannot zoom or lacks contrast.
  • A clean automated score treated as proof of full accessibility.

Do this next

  1. Test the main customer path with a keyboard and zoom.
  2. Run automated checks and review the findings manually.
  3. Fix blockers in forms, navigation, media, and purchase or booking flows first.
  4. Create a way to report an accessibility problem and respond.
